clue.text: River with time becoming source of photos?

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A river and the passing years combine to inspire a photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device that produces photographs, so it is literally their origin; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Hated set of articles by scholar

parts.note: three English articles in a row: the indefinite an and a, then the definite the
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a collection of essays written by an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' looks like pieces of writing, but it means the grammatical words AN, A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Used predicatively, as in 'it is anathema to me', the word describes something utterly detested.

clue.text: Time for all to indicate cross?

definitions.text: Time for all to indicate cross?

parts.words: Time for all to indicate cross?
parts.note: the cross is the X a voter marks on a ballot paper, and the occasion when the whole country does so is the national poll

explanation.surface: A moment when everyone must show they are angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the mark a voter puts on a ballot paper in a nationwide vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationwide poll is the occasion when every voter marks an X beside a candidate on the ballot.

clue.text: Start of furious quarrel over tip? It's stinking

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit above, or over, the last one
the opening letter of the word furious is the only part used

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel
a tip is a filthy, messy place, like a pigsty

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a rubbish dump, and the place reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' is British for a rubbish dump, or any very untidy place; a STY is the same idea. 'It's' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowsty describes a stale, musty, foul-smelling atmosphere, so it is a synonym for smelly.

clue.text: Arrange pr prints differently for argumentative friend

indicators.note: arranged differently tells you the letters of these three words are reshuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A printer is told to lay out the PR material in a new way for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Differently' turns ARRANGE, PR and PRINTS into fifteen new letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's training partner spars with them; the phrase is also used for a friend one enjoys a good argument with.

clue.text: Woman wearing a grand coat

indicators.note: the woman wears the other letters around her like clothing, so they enclose her name

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds, written K for kilo
Nora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is dressed in a very expensive coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' puts A and K around NORA. 'Grand' looks like an adjective but is slang for a thousand, K.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket.

clue.text: Bay, perhaps, blocked by another boat

indicators.note: the required word is boxed in by the letters of the words another boat, which block it on each side

explanation.surface: A bay is obstructed by a second vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' reads as a stretch of coast, which suits the boats, but it is the bay leaf; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay leaves are a culinary seasoning plant, an example of the category.

clue.text: Old man in agony

parts.note: old man is slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: An elderly man is suffering terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme suffering, a synonym of severe hurt.

clue.text: Sign of sadness not originally getting attention

indicators.note: the word loses its original, opening letter

parts.note: a tear shed when crying shows sadness

explanation.surface: Someone's unhappiness goes unnoticed at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not originally' removes the T from TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone your ear is to listen to them, so the word means a hearing or notice.

clue.text: Client, one making jokes heartlessly

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a punster is someone who makes jokes based on puns

explanation.surface: A comedian's customer is cruelly mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' takes out S, the middle letter of PUNSTER. PUNTER is British slang for a customer or a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a punter is a paying customer or someone placing a bet.

clue.text: Soft hat I discarded in the wake of information

indicators.note: following behind, so the hat letters come after the information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the letter is thrown away from the word for hat

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A soft hat is cast aside after some news comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hat' is old slang here, a roof covering worn on the head; 'information' is British slang, and 'in the wake of' means following, so the hat part comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle means mild and tender, a close synonym of soft in manner.

clue.text: Old boy found in drawer tattered clothing

indicators.note: the abbreviation is located inside the other letters
the word drawer is torn up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil's ragged clothes turn up in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' suggests furniture, fitting the clothes, but it is only the letters to be torn up; OB, an old boy, is a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a person's whole collection of clothes as well as the cupboard holding them.

clue.text: Careless talk hit learning and innovative mental activity

indicators.note: carelessly arranged, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Thoughtless chatter damages education, unlike creative thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careless' shuffles TALK, HIT and LEARNING into fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names creative problem-solving that approaches a question from an unexpected angle.

clue.text: Tough head

definitions.meaning: a tough, violent man is called a ..., as in hard ...

explanation.surface: A hard-headed person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard nut is a tough guy, and nut is slang for the skull or brain.

clue.text: Fuss that's normal about exotic veal

indicators.note: the normal word goes around the rearranged meat

parts.note: par is the normal standard, as in feeling below par

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters of veal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner complains about an unusual veal dish being treated as ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR is golf's standard score, hence normal, as in 'feeling below par'; 'exotic' scrambles the veal, which sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is tiresome, elaborate bother over something trivial.

clue.text: Remains from party bachelor left

indicators.note: the bachelor has left, so his letter departs from the party word

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: What is left after the stag party once the groom has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the leftover remains, but it means departed: B leaves BASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the residue left after burning, the remains of a fire or cremation.

clue.text: Nimbleness I inspired in a couple of gymnasts

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces goes inside the letters that follow
a couple means two, so the first two letters of gymnasts are taken

parts.note: lit, as in fired up, describes someone inspired or excited

explanation.surface: A pair of gymnasts motivate the speaker to be more agile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' tempts as the container signal, breathing the I in, but it is LIT, fired up; 'couple of' takes the first two letters, and 'in' puts I + LIT between them, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Agility is the quality of being quick and light on one's feet.

clue.text: Cosmetic tip offered by unusual fool lacking depth

indicators.note: the tip, here the end letter, given by the word unusual
the fool is without the depth letter

parts.note: a dipstick is slang for a stupid person

explanation.surface: A make-up tip comes from a strange, shallow idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip offered by unusual' is the end letter L; 'lacking' removes D from DIPSTICK to leave IPSTICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is a make-up product applied to colour the mouth.

clue.text: Noted dancer mentioned a part of flight

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: one step in a flight of stairs is a stair, with the a kept

explanation.surface: A famous dancer referred to a section of a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred ASTAIRE, the Hollywood dancer, sounds like 'a stair', one step of a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was a celebrated Hollywood tap and ballroom dancer of the 1930s to 1950s.

clue.text: Punish a group of photographers, presumptuous young things?

parts.note: to whip is to punish by flogging
per means a, as in once per day
snappers is slang for press photographers

explanation.surface: Discipline a pack of paparazzi for their cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' gives PER, as in 'ten pence a go' meaning per go.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes impertinent young people who are overconfident for their age.

clue.text: House sailor preferred first

indicators.note: the preferred letters come first, before the sailor

parts.note: pref is the abbreviation for preferred, as in preferred shares
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman chose a particular home over the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the abbreviation PREF goes in front of AB.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated dwelling, many built in Britain after the Second World War.

clue.text: Island streets receiving broadcast

indicators.note: the word is broadcast aloud, so it is heard not spelt

parts.note: roads are streets

explanation.surface: The streets of an island are picking up a radio signal.
explanation.walkthrough: RHODES, the Greek island, sounds like ROADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Teenager spilt healthy drink

indicators.note: the word teenager is spilt and its letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A teenager knocks over a nutritious beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilt' signals that TEENAGER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea, made from unfermented leaves, is widely promoted for its health benefits.

clue.text: Musical group first to last providing hilarious event

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for the group moves to the end

parts.note: a trio is a group of three musicians

explanation.surface: A band puts on a very funny show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to last' moves the T of TRIO to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is informal for something or someone extremely funny, as in 'the party was a riot'.

clue.text: Military display generating rubbish as well

parts.note: tat is shoddy, worthless goods
too means as well, also

explanation.surface: A parade of soldiers also produces junk.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British for cheap tasteless stuff. A TATTOO is an evening military display, such as the Edinburgh Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an outdoor show of drilling and marching bands by soldiers, often at night.

clue.text: Boy at orchard's entrance for fruit

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A lad waits at the orchard gate for some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like the orchard's gate but takes O, the first letter of orchard's.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, the seed-bearing part of the plant.

clue.text: Regret mention of small jumper

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the clue wants a word with the same sound

parts.note: roo is a short form of kangaroo, a jumping animal, and the short form makes it small

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry they brought up a little sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' reads as the British word for a sweater, but it is a kangaroo, ROO, which sounds like RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to wish it had not happened, which is to feel sorry about it.

clue.text: Starters in classy hotel elegantly fashioned — by him?

definitions.text: Starters in classy hotel elegantly fashioned — by him?

indicators.note: the starters are the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The first courses in a smart hotel are beautifully made, and who by?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' suggests first courses, apt for the cook, but it means the first letters of the four words that follow; the whole clue also describes who prepares them.
explanation.definitionFit: The cook in charge of a restaurant kitchen is the one who would prepare such dishes.
